newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Feb 6.

text.p: PRAVO - The railway workers union prolonged the railway strike for another 24 hours after a meeting with Transport Minister Martin Riman on Wednesday did not lead to an agreement. The chairman of the union, Jaromir Dusek, still insists that the strike is legal, despite the ruling of the municipal court in Prague, which ordered railway workers to end the strike.
- Ceska Sporitelna plans to restore its clients' interest in small credits with a new approach which will allow clients to obtain credit up to 30,000 crowns without guarantees.

- The European rating agency IBCA evaluated Investicni a Postovni Banka on Wednesday and gave it a long-term rating of BBB, which is one degree less than the rating given to Ceska Sporitelna, and a short-term rating of A2, which is equal to Ceska Sporitelna's rating.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The leading world bank Solomon Brothers will most probably organise the sale of the state's share in Investicni a Postovni Banka. It should be officially announced tomorrow by the Finance Ministry after an agreement is made concerning the amount Solomon Brothers will be paid.

- According to one of the top 10 world banks, Goldman Sachs, growth of Czech GDP will slow significantly in the next few months. The bank further predicts that the trade deficit will reach 180 billion crowns this year.

- If Konsolidacni Banka buys Komercni Banka's claim of nearly three billion crowns in automotive corporation Tatra, the bank could either capitalise it or sell it. Mercedes and Volkswagon apparently show interest in buying the majority share.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - Farmers, who are continually dissatisfied with the agrarian policy of the cabinet, have taken a radical step. The Czech-Moravian Agrarian Conference, which represents most agricultural entrepeneurs, announced the lowest prices at which they will sell their products, which show an average increase of 30 to 40 percent.
